name: TDC ADMET Caco2_Wang
description: Predict the permeability of a compound through a layer of Caco-2 cells, an in-vitro model of absorption in the human intestine (logarithm of the apparent permeability in cm/s) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint Caco2_Wang of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the mean absolute error on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; lower is better.

sources.locator: ADME Properties Evaluation in Drug Discovery: Prediction of Caco-2 Cell Permeability Using a Combination of NSGA-II and Boosting
Caco-2 (Cell Effective Permeability), Wang et al.: regression, 906 drugs, reference Wang et al. 2016 JCIM 56(4).

Huang et al. (2022), Artificial intelligence foundation for therapeutic science (Nat Chem Biol): the Therapeutics Data Commons paper linked from the TDC site, benchmark paper only; also arXiv 2102.09548, Therapeutics Data Commons: Machine Learning Datasets and Tasks for Drug Discovery and Development.

requirements.datasets: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: the predicted value. train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the mean absolute error on the test part, minimized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet

limitations: Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
The record was found in a hashed snapshot of its source; it is not replayed. See VALIDITY.md.

science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it. Using a task to evaluate an agent, framework, or general-purpose model, or citing only a benchmark, dataset, or tool, does not establish scientific importance.
science_relevance.reason: The cited paper(s) have the prediction or measurement of this property as their main objective; the task scores a structure-based predictor of the same property.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the logarithm of the apparent Caco-2 cell permeability (cm/s) of a drug-like molecule from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Caco-2 monolayers are the standard in vitro model of intestinal absorption, so predicting permeability from structure screens candidate compounds for oral uptake before synthesis.

papers.title: ADME Properties Evaluation in Drug Discovery: Prediction of Caco-2 Cell Permeability Using a Combination of NSGA-II and Boosting
papers.task_relation: The task predicts the Caco-2 permeability of the 906-compound set that this paper assembled and modelled; the local split, metric and candidate freedom differ from the paper's.
papers.primary_goal: Build a predictive model of Caco-2 cell permeability from molecular structure, using a multi-objective genetic algorithm for descriptor selection and boosting.
